page: Amazon Web Services m2.4xlarge is an earlier-generation instance provisioned on the Xen hypervisor, driven by an Intel Xeon E5-2665 processor operating at 2.4 GHz. It features 8 dedicated physical cores and 8 vCPUs on the x86_64 architecture. Hardware instruction extensions such as AVX, AVX-512, and AES are absent. The platform integrates 68.0 GB of system memory, yielding 8.55 GB per core, along with 1680 GB of attached local HDD storage, 1 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, and zero GPUs.

Benchmark evaluations show modest compute capabilities reflecting the age of the underlying architecture. Single-core processing is limited, demonstrated by a Geekbench single-core score of 662.0 and a stress-ng single-core score of 1229.78. Multi-threaded processing reaches average tiers in stress-ng multi-core testing at 6556.53 and Clang software compilation at 6139.0. Static web serving throughput reaches 5.88 GB/sec and Redis SET performance delivers 1.56 million operations per second. Memory throughput remains consistent with its generation, achieving average scores with 49.87 GB/sec large-block read bandwidth and 39.26 GB/sec large-block write bandwidth.

The instance trades compute efficiency and cryptographic instruction sets for high memory allocation per core and bulk local magnetic storage. It suits memory-oriented batch processing, non-latency-sensitive database operations, and internal caching systems that do not rely on modern vector acceleration or high-speed solid-state I/O.
description: Amazon Web Services m2.4xlarge is a legacy virtual server featuring 8 dedicated vCPUs on an Intel Xeon E5-2665 processor clocked at 2.4 GHz on the Xen hypervisor. The instance is configured with 68.0 GB of system memory, providing 8.55 GB per vCPU, alongside 1680 GB of local HDD storage and a 1 Gbps network baseline. It contains no dedicated GPUs and lacks modern vector extensions like AVX and AES. Performance benchmarks show constrained single-core compute performance, highlighted by lower-tier Geekbench and compression results, though multi-core throughput and memory bandwidth measure in average ranges. The hardware configuration emphasizes large RAM capacity and local magnetic capacity over processing speed. This profile makes the instance viable for memory-heavy legacy enterprise applications, batch reporting jobs, and secondary database staging environments that require significant system memory without modern CPU acceleration requirements.
